newsitem.title: MEXICO: Right-wing PAN snatches two Mexican states.
newsitem.headline: Right-wing PAN snatches two Mexican states.

text.p: Mexico's conservative opposition National Action Party (PAN) said on Monday it had won two of six state governorships from the long-ruling PRI, including Nuevo Leon, the country's industrial heartland.
The results dealt another blow to the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which sustained heavy losses in the lower house of Congress and lost the high-profile post of Mexico City's mayor.

PAN officials said they had taken governorships from the PRI in Nuevo Leon, whose capital Monterrey is a vibrant business centre. They also took the central state of Queretaro in Sunday's mid-term elections.
While the PRI claimed victory in tiny Colima state, in Mexico's southwest, it conceded the Queretaro setback on Monday.
But in poverty-stricken Campeche state, left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) activists took to the streets to protest preliminary official election results that put the PRI ahead.
"We will not stop until every last one of the votes has been counted," said PRD governor candidate Layda Sansores San Roman.

"Right now, we are going to start a political mobilisation (against the count)," she said, calling on party supporters to protest results in districts where fraud had allegedly been detected. "In Campeche everyone voted, even the dead."
Partial preliminary official results from Campeche gave the PRI 47.76 percent of the vote against 40.83 for the PRD.
Fernando Canales Clariond, the PAN's candidate in Nuevo Leon, claimed victory at a midnight news conference after preliminary results shaped up in his favour.
Almost complete results showed the PRI retaining the northern Sonora state, with 41.49 percent of the vote against the PAN's 32.98 percent and the PRD's 22.5 with 93 percent of of votes counted.
Results have yet to come in from the central state of San Luis Potosi.
If the two PAN victories are confirmed they would give the pro-business party a total of six state governorships. The party already holds Jalisco, Baja California, Chihuahua and Guanajuato.

The PRI has held almost total power in Mexico for 68 years, including the presidency, majority control of congress and most governorships. The PRI looked likely to lose its majority control of congress, partial results showed Monday.
